title: adaptive-schema-coercion-and-runtime-hints-for-structured-output
author: Priya Patel
release_notes: Introduces adaptive schema coercion hints and a deprecation path for strict_mode boolean; runtime supports per-request strictness levels (warn/relaxed/reject) and streaming-safe soft-coercion with mapped error codes.
commits: feat(response): add runtime 'schema_coercion_hint' metadata and coercion engine (pri)
refactor(response): extract strictness enum and deprecate strict_mode boolean
test(response): unit+integration for streaming coercion and error mapping
docs: document new 'strictness' enum and upgrade guide for OpenAI-compat responses
perf: ensure batching unaffected by coercion checks via fast-paths
description: Motivation: We want structured outputs (response_format/jsonschema) to be practical in the wild: models occasionally emit slightly mismatched types or nested nulls which today either cause full stream rejection (strict_mode=true) or silent acceptance (strict_mode=false). This PR adds adaptive coercion hints and runtime-level strictness controls to reduce operational failures while preserving strong validation options for teams that need them. Design summary: 1) Introduce a new per-request 'strictness' enum that replaces/deprecates the boolean strict_mode. Values: 'reject' (current strict behavior), 'warn' (validate but allow soft coercions during streaming and emit structured errors), 'relaxed' (coerce common mismatches). 2) Add 'schema_coercion_hint' metadata to the response_format payload schema which is a lightweight descriptor (max 1KB) that the serving runtime uses to prefer specific coercion strategies without altering schema semantics. Examples: number-as-string coercion, empty-string->null, boolean-like strings. 3) Streaming behavior: coercion is applied incrementally when safe; ambiguous coercions are emitted as structured 'coercion_warning' events in the stream and final validation will either pass with warnings or fail with an 'schema_violation' error depending on strictness. 4) Error mapping: we standardized new error codes under openai-compat layer (Schema.CoercionWarning, Schema.Violation, Schema.StreamTruncated) and mapped them to human-readable messages; the API surface still returns the OpenAI-compatible status codes but includes 'redwood_error' for more detail. 5) Backwards compatibility: the boolean 'strict_mode' is still accepted for this release and mapped to strictness (strict_mode=true -> 'reject', false->'relaxed') with a deprecation warning in logs and docs. 6) Telemetry: added counters and latency buckets to ensure coercion hot-paths are observable and to detect regressions in per-token latency. Implementation notes: - Core coercion engine implemented in src/core/response/coercion with a compact rule table and fast-path for common cases to avoid adding extra allocations in the hot loop. - Streaming validator hooks placed in streaming_validator.go; they emit structured stream events which the OpenAI compatibility layer forwards as chunked meta events. - SDKs: convenience helpers added to Python and TypeScript SDKs to set 'strictness' and to parse 'coercion_warning' events when streaming. - Docs: upgrade guide for teams converting from strict_mode boolean to strictness enum, and sample recipes for tool/function-calling owners to choose policies per route. Tests & CI: initial run triggered a flaky integration test in response_format_integration.sh due to a timeout in perf-canary; I fixed the test by reducing a synthetic latency injection and restructured the test harness to decouple coercion verification from end-to-end bandwidth variables. Final CI status: all checks passed (unit, integration, lint, mypy, ts-check, e2e-canary). Review summary: - Evan requested clearer telemetry tags (added 'coercion.rule' and 'coercion.outcome'). - Marina asked for more explicit decoupling between function-calling payloads and coercion rules; added a guard that disables coercion for tool-call payloads unless route opts-in. - Derek raised perf concerns; added microbenchmarks and optimized the fast-path allocation to remove measurable regressions in the 95th percentile. - Small followups scheduled: ENG-4990 to add a visual indicator in Redwood Console for per-route coercion failure rate and PM task to evaluate default strictness per template. Migration & rollout: feature gated under 'response.adaptive_coercion' with rollout plan: 1) enable in staging for 48h, 2) enable in canary shard with 1% traffic for 7 days, 3) global opt-in for hosted teams via API flag, 4) allow Dedicated/Private customers to set default via their config. Observability & alerting: added a P99 latency alert for coercion path in observability/telemetry-metrics.yaml and a regression alert if coercion-related errors increase >5% over baseline. Related work: ties to ENG-4921 (streaming stability) and SUP-1173 (support escalations where strict_mode caused production outages). Docs and examples updated to include migration steps and sample prompts. Merge notes: squashed and merged after approvals; release notes added.
review_comments: Evan Li: Please add coercion rule telemetry tags so we can filter by rule type in logs. Can you also add unit test coverage for numeric-string coercion edgecases?
Priya Patel (author): Added 'coercion.rule' and 'coercion.outcome' tags; pushed tests for numeric-string and empty-string->null cases.
Marina Raskin: Ensure function-calling payloads are not coerced by default; tool outputs may be JSON-lit and authors expect strict typing.
Priya Patel (author): Added route opt-in guard and documented the change. Default remains conservative for function/tool calls.
Derek Zhou: Microbenchmark showed a small regression at 95th pct — can we avoid extra allocations?
Priya Patel (author): Optimized fast-path, replaced one allocation with stack buffer; reran bench and P95 matches baseline.
